title: Temp File Cleanup Signals
description: Contract for the stale scratch-file sweep run from the startup hook (#2771). This is the one startup step that MUTATES the tree, so the constraints below are deliberately tighter than a configuration file would otherwise carry: they exist to bound what a future edit to the data file can select for deletion.

patterns.description: Basename globs matched against DIRECT CHILDREN of the project root. `*` and `?` only — character classes and brace expansion are deliberately unsupported, because every construct added here widens what a config edit can select in a helper that deletes. Each entry must also appear in the project .gitignore; a pattern selecting committed files would make the tracked-file skip the common path rather than the exception it is meant to be.

items.description: At least three literal characters before any wildcard, and no path separator anywhere. The literal-prefix floor means a one-character typo cannot turn a scoped pattern into one matching everything at the project root; the separator ban means no pattern can reach outside it.

minAgeMs.description: A file is stale when `now - mtime >= minAgeMs`; the boundary belongs to the stale side, so a file exactly at the threshold is removed. Floor of one hour, deliberately: a threshold near zero would delete scratch files belonging to a command running right now in this session or a peer session sharing the working directory, which is the one failure mode this sweep must never cause. The shipped value is one day (86400000).

reportWhenNothingRemoved.description: Whether the startup block emits a `Trash:` row when the sweep removed nothing and nothing failed. False in the shipped file: a clean sweep emits no row, matching the Peers row's `none` and the dependency check's healthy state. Set true only when diagnosing whether the sweep is running at all.

rationale.description: Why each threshold holds the value it does. Not read at runtime, but kept in the data file rather than only in the schema so an editor changing a number sees the reasoning next to it.
